chapter: Club Alabam and the Europe contract
title: Refusing to play blues for the Edison Company
summary: The Edison man wants blues, not Wooding's arrangements, and Wooding refuses to be held to it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Right. Now, was it while you were at the Club Alabam that you started appearing on records, or made the --

Well, I had a chance to make records, but I didn't go, I didn't take it. Because, I went to the Edison Company, I'll never forget that. They sent for us to come down there to make records. This was at the Nest, before I left the Nest. And this fellow, when we started, we started playing one of these numbers like "Covered Wagon" or something like that. And this fellow said, "Look, I can get Paul Whiteman or Paul Specht to play that. What I want you to hear, play me some blues."
Well I told him what he could hold a rope and down out, and do to it.
